Audited every claim directly from graph-distance, separator, tree-decomposition, and planarity definitions.
Created and ran <workspace-home>/paired_targeted_stress_v2_scratch/targeted_barbados_p31_geodesic_separator/audit-baseline/exact_graph_audit.py using only integer graph operations.
The checker certified the icosahedral embedding, diameter 3, all 794 deletions of at most four vertices, all 162 geodesic vertex sets, and the explicit balanced two-geodesic witness.

claims.claim: It suffices to treat connected nonempty graphs.
claims.evidence: For nonempty G, if every component has order at most n/2, deleting any two available geodesics cannot enlarge a component. Otherwise there is a unique component H of order greater than n/2. Applying the connected result inside H leaves pieces of order at most |H|/2<=n/2, while every other component has order at most n-|H|<n/2. A path inside H has the same distance in H and G.
claims.search_method: Direct case split on the largest connected component.
claims.witness: Use the two geodesics obtained in the unique component H larger than n/2; if no such H exists, any two trivial geodesics suffice.

claims.claim: Balancedness is monotone under enlarging the deleted set.
claims.evidence: For X contained in Y, every component of G-Y lies in a component of G-X. Its vertex count, and likewise its total nonnegative weight, therefore cannot increase.

claims.claim: In a connected graph, every set X of at most four vertices is contained in the union of two geodesics.
claims.evidence: Partition X into at most two groups of size at most two. Join the two vertices of each two-element group by a shortest path; a singleton is covered by its length-zero geodesic. Empty groups can be replaced by any trivial geodesic. Thus the two path vertex sets contain X.
claims.witness: A pairing of the vertices of X followed by shortest paths for the two pairs.

claims.claim: Any graph having a half-balanced vertex separator of order at most four satisfies the two-geodesic conclusion; the same statement holds for arbitrary nonnegative vertex weights.
claims.evidence: If no original component has more than half the total weight, arbitrary geodesics work. Otherwise the unique overweight component H contains the relevant portion X∩H of the given separator. It has at most four vertices and is covered by two H-geodesics. Their union contains X∩H, so monotonicity keeps every resulting component at most half the original total; other original components were already smaller than half. H-geodesics are G-geodesics.
claims.search_method: Direct weighted component case split combined with the four-vertex cover.
claims.witness: Two shortest paths covering X in the connected case, or X∩H in the unique overweight component.

claims.claim: Every nonnegatively weighted finite tree has a centroid node whose deletion leaves tree components of weight at most half the total.
claims.evidence: Orient an edge toward a side of weight greater than half, when such a side exists. Each node has at most one outgoing edge because the components on its incident sides are disjoint. Following outgoing edges in a finite tree terminates at a node t. No component of T-t can exceed half the total, since its incident edge would then point outward from t.
claims.witness: The terminal node t of the heavy-side orientation.

claims.claim: Every vertex-weighted graph tree decomposition has a half-balanced bag.
claims.evidence: Assign every graph vertex and its weight to one bag containing it, and take a centroid t of the resulting weighted decomposition tree. If K is a component of G-B_t, every bag-subtree belonging to a vertex of K avoids t. Adjacent vertices have intersecting bag-subtrees, so connectivity puts all those subtrees and assigned bags in one component R of T-t. Hence w(K) is at most the assigned weight of R, which is at most half the total.
claims.search_method: Direct tree-decomposition running-intersection and centroid proof.
claims.witness: The bag B_t indexed by a centroid t after assigning each vertex weight to one containing bag.

claims.claim: If a connected graph has a tree decomposition in which every bag is contained in the union of two geodesics of the original graph, then those geodesics yield a half-balanced separator for every nonnegative vertex weighting.
claims.evidence: Choose the half-balanced bag B_t from claim 5 and two original-graph geodesics whose union contains it. Deleting this larger set cannot increase any remaining component's nonnegative weight, so their union is half-balanced.
claims.search_method: Composition of the balanced-bag theorem with deletion monotonicity.
claims.witness: The two geodesics covering the centroid bag B_t.

claims.claim: Every graph of treewidth at most three satisfies the target, even with arbitrary nonnegative vertex weights; planarity is unnecessary.
claims.evidence: A width-three decomposition has bags of size at most four, and claim 2 covers every such bag by two original-graph geodesics when the graph is connected. Claims 5 and 6 then give weighted half-balance. For a disconnected weighted graph, either it is already balanced or the same argument is applied to its unique component of weight greater than half; treewidth is inherited by components.
claims.search_method: Treewidth bag-size reduction plus the weighted disconnected-component argument.
claims.witness: Two geodesics covering a centroid bag of a width-three decomposition.

claims.claim: In particular, every outerplanar graph and every planar graph with a universal vertex satisfies the target.
claims.evidence: Every outerplanar graph has treewidth at most two: after outerplanar completion, the triangular bounded faces of each maximal block yield three-vertex decomposition bags, with trivial small blocks handled separately. If v is universal in a planar graph, deleting v from a plane embedding leaves all other vertices incident with the face formed by removing v and its edges, so G-v is outerplanar. Adding v to every width-two bag gives a width-three decomposition of G. Claim 7 applies in both cases.
claims.search_method: Outerplanar decomposition and universal-vertex embedding reduction.
claims.witness: Three-vertex face bags for an outerplanar completion; add the universal vertex to every bag in the second case.

claims.claim: If the largest component of an n-vertex graph has order m<=floor(n/2)+4, then the target holds. Consequently every nonempty graph on at most eight vertices satisfies it.
claims.evidence: If m<=floor(n/2), the graph is already balanced. Otherwise H is the unique largest component and d=m-floor(n/2) lies in {1,2,3,4}. Deleting any d vertices of H leaves at most floor(n/2) vertices of H in total, and every other component has at most n-m<=floor(n/2) vertices. Claims 2 and 3 convert this separator into two geodesics. For n<=8, m<=n<=floor(n/2)+4. The checker verified the integer boundary for orders 1 through 9.
claims.search_method: Exact integer inequality proof with a boundary-value checker.
claims.witness: Any d=m-floor(n/2) vertices of the unique oversized component H.

claims.claim: The preceding eight-vertex bound is sharp without planarity.
claims.evidence: In K_n every geodesic has at most two vertices, so two geodesics delete at most four vertices. For n>=9 their complement is a connected clique of order at least n-4, and 2(n-4)>n exactly when n>8. The checker independently enumerated all 45 geodesic vertex sets and all 2025 ordered path-set pairs in K9 and rejected every pair.
claims.search_method: Exact characterization of complete-graph geodesics plus exhaustive K9 enumeration.
claims.witness: K9, and more generally K_n for every n>=9.

claims.claim: A connected graph satisfies the target whenever it has a half-balanced five-vertex separator X for which G[X] contains an induced path a-b-c.
claims.evidence: The edges ab and bc exist while ac does not, so a-b-c is a length-two shortest path. A shortest path between the other two vertices of X supplies the second geodesic. Their union contains X, and deletion monotonicity preserves half-balance.
claims.witness: P1=a-b-c and a shortest path P2 joining the two vertices of X outside {a,b,c}.

claims.claim: A half-balanced isometric cycle is sufficient, regardless of its length.
claims.evidence: Partition the cyclic vertex order into two contiguous blocks differing in size by at most one. Each block arc has length at most floor(|C|/2). On an isometric cycle that arc length equals the distance in G between its endpoints, so both arcs are geodesics. They cover V(C), whose deletion is balanced by hypothesis.
claims.witness: The two nearly equal contiguous block arcs of the isometric cycle.

claims.claim: In a planar graph, the vertex set of every half-balanced 5-cycle is coverable by two geodesics. A half-balanced induced cycle of length six is also coverable in any graph.
claims.evidence: For a 5-cycle, if every consecutive two-edge arc had adjacent endpoints, its five cycle edges and five distance-two chords would form a K5 subgraph, contradicting planarity. A triple whose endpoint chord is absent is therefore a length-two geodesic, while the remaining two cycle vertices form an edge-geodesic. For an induced 6-cycle, two disjoint consecutive triples cover the cycle; each is geodesic because its endpoints are nonadjacent.
claims.search_method: Forbidden-K5 argument for length five and induced-chord argument for length six.
claims.witness: A chordless consecutive triple plus the opposite cycle edge for C5; two consecutive three-vertex blocks for an induced C6.

claims.claim: A balanced union of three specified geodesics need not have a balanced two-member subunion, even in a planar graph.
claims.evidence: The stated graph is a 6-cycle with pendant leaves and is planar. It has n=3m+6. Deleting all three specified pendant edges leaves three components of order m. Deleting any two leaves a component of order 2m+2, and 2(2m+2)-(3m+6)=m-2>0 for m>=3. The replacement pair at a and b leaves largest component m+4, with (3m+6)-2(m+4)=m-2>=0. The checker reproduced these component sizes and exact inequalities.
claims.search_method: Symbolic component counting supplemented by exact graph checks.
claims.witness: For any integer m>=3, use the cycle a-x-b-y-c-z-a, m-1 leaves at each of a,b,c, leaves x',y',z', and specified paths xx', yy', zz'.

claims.claim: There is an explicit 12-vertex planar graph I of diameter three that remains connected after deletion of any four vertices.
claims.evidence: The specified graph has 12 vertices, 30 edges, and the 20 stated triangular faces. The checker verified every edge has two face incidences, every vertex link is a cycle, and V-E+F=2, certifying the sphere embedding. Integer BFS gave diameter 3. Exhaustive checking of all 1+12+66+220+495=794 deletion sets of size at most four found the remaining 12-|X| vertices connected every time.
claims.search_method: Explicit combinatorial-embedding certification, exact BFS, and exhaustive subset enumeration.
claims.witness: The graph with poles N,S, cycles u_0...u_4 and l_0...l_4, and edges Nu_i, Sl_i, u_i u_{i+1}, l_i l_{i+1}, u_i l_i, u_i l_{i-1}, with indices modulo five.

claims.claim: The planar graph I has no half-balanced separator formed by one geodesic.
claims.evidence: Diameter 3 limits a geodesic to at most four vertices. Claim 15 then makes I-V(P) connected, with at least 8 vertices, exceeding half of 12. Independently, the checker enumerated all 162 distinct geodesic vertex sets and verified that every deletion leaves a single component larger than 6.
claims.search_method: Deduction from diameter/connectivity plus exhaustive enumeration of shortest-path vertex sets.
claims.witness: The 12-vertex graph I; every one-geodesic deletion leaves one component of order at least eight.

claims.claim: Two geodesics do half-balance I, so the preceding result establishes genuine necessity of the second path rather than a counterexample to the target.
claims.evidence: Both displayed paths have length three. The endpoint neighborhoods of u_3 and l_0 are disjoint and the endpoints are nonadjacent, so their distance is three and both paths are geodesics. Their union deletes exactly N,u_0,u_1,u_2,u_3,l_0. The checker found that the remaining six vertices form one component, exactly meeting the half-balance threshold.
claims.search_method: Exact BFS and component check of the explicit path pair.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a half-balanced union of two original-graph geodesics in every finite simple unweighted planar graph. The draft proves material but proper special cases: treewidth at most three, outerplanar graphs, planar graphs with a universal vertex, graphs of order at most eight, and several separator configurations. Its obstruction families only rule out simpler approaches and do not give a planar counterexample to the two-geodesic statement. Thus it does not resolve the universal target, but its final writeup explicitly says so and labels the result PARTIAL; that claimed resolution is accurate.
